title: Ten plagues: summary and the puzzle of hardening
english: The story of the [[ten plagues >> Bible:Exodus 7-12]] is known to the whole world: Egypt and Pharaoh are beaten with signs until a freeborn people, forced into slavery, is restored to liberty. Aaron’s rod becomes a serpent and swallows the magicians’ serpents; still [[Pharaoh’s heart was hardened >> Bible:Exodus 7:13]]. Sometimes Scripture says the heart “was hardened,” sometimes [[the Lord hardened Pharaoh’s heart >> Bible:Exodus 9:12]]. The careful reader must not rush past that difference.
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Heine FOTC 71.

title: Divine letters demand spiritual reading
english: If we believe these letters divine, they are written for our training, not as antique gossip. Hardening does not make God the author of evil; it discloses judgment. The same sun softens wax and hardens mud: one working, different effects according to the matter that receives it.
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Heine FOTC 71.

title: Magicians’ mimicry and the limits of Egypt
english: The magicians can mimic as far as the [[gnats >> Bible:Exodus 8:18-19]]; beyond that they fail and confess [[“This is the finger of God” >> Bible:Exodus 8:19]]. Demonic power is finite; God’s signs increase. So the church must distinguish flashy imitation from the truth that alone liberates.
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Heine FOTC 71.

title: First difference: who hardens, and when
english: We noted another difference: in earlier strokes the heart “is hardened”; when ulcers break the magicians’ stand, Scripture speaks more terribly — [[the Lord hardened Pharaoh’s heart >> Bible:Exodus 9:12]]. Judgment escalates as resistance deepens.
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Heine FOTC 71.

title: The Spirit that filled Moses
english: Who is filled with the Spirit that filled Moses? Not every talkative tongue. The Spirit of wisdom and might drives God’s work against Egypt — that is, against the vices that enslave the soul.
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Heine FOTC 71.

title: Moses sent back into Egypt
english: Moses is sent back into Egypt to work the wonders God put in his hand. So too, if we have left Egypt in mind, we return in word to brothers still enslaved — not to make Egypt pleasant, but to call a people out.
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Heine FOTC 71.

title: Voices, hail, and blows from above
english: Then come blows from above: [[voices, thunder, hail and fire >> Bible:Exodus 9:23-26]] wasting Egypt while Goshen is spared. Fear the One who turns both sky and sea to judgment — and still makes a difference for his own.
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Heine FOTC 71.

title: Moral Egypt within — Homilia IV CLOSEOUT
english: Morally Egypt is in us, and Pharaoh the princely power of vice. The plagues are God’s corrections: they soften a receiving heart and harden a resisting one. The [[firstborn >> Bible:Exodus 12:29]] to be put to death are sin’s first movements. Let us not harden our hearts, that the people within may go free. Amen.
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Heine FOTC 71.
